questions.problem: Let $F(x)={x}^{2}-2x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **odd** extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ What is $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,0)?$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [0,\pi ),$ the odd extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}F(x), & x\in [0,\pi ), \\ -F(-x), & x\in (-\pi ,0).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, for $x\in (-\pi ,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-F(-x) \\  & =-((-x)^{2}-2(-x)) \\  & =-({x}^{2}+2x) \\  & =-{x}^{2}-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $F(x)=-3x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ Select the correct missing parts in the Fourier sine series of the **odd** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of the function $F(x)$ below.

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot {{field-2}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=-3x$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{b}_{n}=-\frac{6}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }x\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =-\frac{6}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =-\frac{6}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{n}[x\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{6}{n\pi }((\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0))-\frac{1}{n}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =\frac{6}{n\pi }(\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\frac{1}{n}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))) \\  & =\frac{6\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )}{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{6(-1)^{n}}{n}.
$$

Finally, the Fourier sine series is

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{6(-1)^{n}}{n}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(nx).
$$

questions.worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [0,12),$ the odd extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}F(x), & x\in [0,12), \\ -F(-x), & x\in (-12,0).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, for $x\in (-12,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-F(-x) \\  & =-((-x)^{2}-6(-x)) \\  & =-({x}^{2}+6x) \\  & =-{x}^{2}-6x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-4) & =-(-4)^{2}-6(-4)=8.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $F(x)=-3x+2$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ Select the correct missing parts in the Fourier sine series of the **odd** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of the function $F(x)$ below.

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot {{field-2}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=-3x+2$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(-3x+2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=-3x+2\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=-3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =\frac{2}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{n}[(-3x+2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{3}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =-\frac{2}{n\pi }(((-3\pi +2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))+\frac{3}{n}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =-\frac{2}{n\pi }((-3\pi +2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-2+\frac{3}{n}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))) \\  & =-\frac{2}{n\pi }((-3\pi +2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-2).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{b}_{n}=-\frac{2}{n\pi }((-3\pi +2)(-1)^{n}-2)=\frac{2}{n\pi }((-1)^{n}(3\pi -2)+2).
$$

Finally, the Fourier sine series is

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2}{n\pi }((-1)^{n}(3\pi -2)+2)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(nx).
$$

questions.problem: Let $F(x)={x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+8$ for $x\in [0,\pi ),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **odd** extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ What is $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,0)?$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [0,\pi ),$ the odd extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}F(x), & x\in [0,\pi ), \\ -F(-x), & x\in (-\pi ,0).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, for $x\in (-\pi ,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-F(-x) \\  & =-((-x)^{3}-2(-x)^{2}+8) \\  & =-(-{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+8) \\  & ={x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-8.\end{aligned}
$$
